utterances.text: The only thing I know about the guardhouse is that when I was captured and tied down, somebody shouted, They're done for. I apologise, but I have to say, Fuck their Chetnik mother. And that's when the withdrawal began, once that house fell.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: And do you know what was used to destroy the guardhouse?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I not know? Because that is the reason why they buried me. Everything inside was destroyed by Zoljas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, how was the -- if you could, in brief, just tell us what weapon was used to destroy the guardhouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's just told you, the Zoljas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Do you recall a discussion about a rocket launcher being used at any point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: A Zolja is a rocket launcher, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I just want to use the correct term. He's previously testified about the rocket launcher. I want to stick to the same word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand. What kind of a launcher are you talking about? The ones that Muslims used us or that we used the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, at this point I'll just leave this subject matter alone. Let's go to the looting that you were just testifying about. You testified that and agreed that the people were out of control and that they were taking property. And on your examination yesterday you testified that there was someone who was taking a cow and that the soldier or the soldiers were assisting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the only thing that I could see exactly on that day. I know the man; I don't know his name. And it was over and done with. The soldiers were helping. The cow was very strong and he couldn't do it by himself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. Can you explain to me Ms. Richardson if he said yesterday why he needs to repeat it on re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wanted to be clear that in fact the soldiers were assisting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he said it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's fine. At this time, Your Honour, I don't have any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Richardson. Judge Brydensholt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: I have only one question. When the Muslim village, Zanjevo, was burned in down in June 1992 you said it was your people who did it. But who was it? Was it people from Fakovici participating in the burning down of this Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not burned on one day; this was burned by the villagers. They would burn hay in the fields in order to scare us in Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: So does that mean that it was the Muslims themselves who burned this Muslim village down in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: It's not quite clear to me who did it then. Who set fire to those houses?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: But was it soldiers or the village guard from your village? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier that you usually they would get drunk, the villagers, go down to Fakovici, and then on the way home they would burn one by one, and that's how the houses burnt. A few of them stayed whole, stayed intact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I would like to address just one issue. During your -- when you have been taken to prison in Srebrenica, in these 11 days have you been told at any time for what reason you are -- you have been captured and are kept there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And now have you been told during this time how long it will last, that you would be kept for only a short time or that could go on longer? Or didn't they say anything?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't know anything and nobody said anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And when have you been informed that you will be exchanged? Was it shortly before the exchange or was it announced for some time, hours, days?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What happened was that that morning we were told, Get out and wash yourselves, and then you will go for the exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Judge Eser. I have got very few questions. The first one arises from one of the questions that has been put to you by Judge Eser. You were not told why you were being kept in the prison there, you said. Were you actually charged -- one moment. One you actually charged at any time with any crime while you were there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would I have been charged? What for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just answer yes or no, otherwise you will have to come again tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This Zulfo, do you know -- after this event of your arrest and detention in the prison in Srebrenica, did you ever see this Zulfo again in your life?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a photo of this person?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen him on television?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We don't have the TV programmes from the Federation or from Republika Srpska. All the TV stations that we receive are from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you described a person who came to your cell four times, saying that he was Naser Oric. And you told us you had never seen this person before.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a photo of this person since you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a picture of him on any newspaper?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen a shot of him in -- on television?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you ever shown a photo of him by any officer of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if I were to bring this person here in front of you today, would you be able to recognise him?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, but you must know that that happened 12 years ago. I have changed and he must have changed, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you assure me that in these 12 years you have never seen a picture of this person?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have not seen anything on Naser. I have never, never seen anything in relation to him personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know which trial this is, who is the accused in this trial?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could conclude that it is Naser, because I was in the prison in Srebrenica. Otherwise, there would be no way for me to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But when was it the first -- when was the first time that you heard a certain Naser Oric had been charged before this Tribunal -- accused before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did you hear about it? When did you hear about the arrest and the charging of Naser Oric before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard -- I can't remember exactly when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How did you come to know about it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You did not see it on TV? You did not watch it on TV?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB ZIKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, not personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I have no further questions. That basically means that your testimony comes to an end here. Mr. Zikic, on behalf of Judge Brydensholt and Judge Eser, but also on behalf of the Tribunal and my own behalf of course, I would like to thank you for accepted to come over and give testimony in this case. It has been a long testimony; I'm sure you are very tired. You will soon be free --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will soon be free to go back to your country. In fact Mr. Usher will escort you out of this courtroom. I assure you that you will receive all the assistance you require to enable you to return to your country soon. On behalf of everyone present here, I would like to wish you a safe journey home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, while we are still here there is no way we can conclude the rest because we have an occasion where we have to bid a goodbye to a member of my team and we had arranged everything to happen at 2.00. So we cannot do that. Unless you can finish all the housekeeping matters in less than ten minutes and of course given that everyone behind the dark glass agrees. I don't know that you can finish everything in less than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The Prosecution, really, we don't have so much by way of housekeeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Neither do we, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's going to deal with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: First we have the scheduling of the witnesses for the month of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, the scheduling.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I'll ask the usher please to assist me. And the second issue is, Your Honour, that you asked for a clarification whether or not it's possible to do some estimation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Roughly, yes, for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Roughly for the time being. It will be that we come out with an estimation of the third week of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway. Okay. Point taken, Mr. Wubben. Perhaps you could in the course of the holiday, the recess, itemise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that we can then see whether we can intervene, whether it's the case of intervening or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I will give the floor to Mr. Di Fazio --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- in order to address two minor issues, also limited in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, if Your Honours please. Two witnesses on the January list, relatives of deceased in this case and mentioned in the indictment. One is the wife of Mr. Milavanovic, the other is the father of Mr. Dokic. I think the -- I don't have the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, 24 and 26. MR. DI FAZIO: You can see. I don't know to what extent the Defence want to put us to proof on the issue of death of those two victims -- I'm not talking about the manner of death but the circumstances of death. And it seems to the Prosecution that those two particular witnesses might be ripe for agreement. So all I wanted to do is place on the record the Prosecution's invitation to the Defence to consider those two statements and notify us whether or not they might be -- they might consent to those statements being tendered into evidence and obviate the need to call those two people. If they were to come here they would be brief. I don't need an answer, but I want the Court and the Defence know and they can let us know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next. MR. DI FAZIO: The next issue, relating to the document that was produced. I had all sorts of documents I wanted to take you through; I don't need to do that. I think I can simply take you to my conclusion. Mr. Nikolic produced, as you remember, a crumpled piece of paper out of his pocket. That was, as I understand, D114.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't remember. MR. DI FAZIO: That's what it was because you asked him or Mr. Jones asked you and does it have the words with Razmija and no date at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And if you look at various documentation, that fits. I didn't know about the other copy or version, shall we say, which is P69. I should have known about it, but I didn't. I thought I was producing the document for the first time. A document that I thought I had proofed Mr. Nikolic on was in fact D114.1 or had bearing ERN number 02075708. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the document you had given him? MR. DI FAZIO: That's the document I had given him. The reason I gave it to him is he was interested and had become emotional about it during the proofing. It wasn't for proofing purposes. So what he pulled out of his pocket may, as he says, been given to him by the other person concerned, and you recall that some days later Ms. Vidovic cross-examined about that. So you're left with that; or you hear from me that I also provided him with that document. I've made inquiries with the investigators. We've handled those two witnesses. They assure me that no documentation or bits of evidence have ever been given to any witness, including those two particular witnesses. So there we have it. That's all that I can explain. I hope that goes to satisfy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We of course have no comments on that. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, well, I understand from Mr. Di Fazio's answer that that was the only document that was given to Mr. Nikolic. We would still like to know when and where it was given, whether it was given in the field, in Kravica, and whether he was told anything when given the document. Because he seemed to think it was an indictment against him. MR. DI FAZIO: It was given to him in my office prior to testifying, not in the field. He wasn't told it was an indictment or charge. Your Honour asked that. I think, from my recollection of the transcript, he himself produced it and said that in answer to a question of this is the charge [sic]. But he certainly wasn't told that because it's simply not so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, from our side we don't really have any housekeeping apart from one very minor thing which is we might be filing a motion tomorrow. It doesn't require urgent action by the Chamber, but we want to just be sure that some of your staff were still here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, of course. Plus I can assure you to put your mind at rest, both of you, I use electronic signatures -- I have an electronic signature which I can use while I am at home for my holidays. In other words, if there needs to be some urgent motion to be decided, we will of course be in contact and it can be drafted and signed by me and sent over electronically here. So there is never the problem of having an urgent motion not being able to be decided while we are in the recess. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, only out of courtesy if my learned friend can provide us with a courtesy copy of this filing beforehand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's not finalised yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May we know what it is about?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Rule 68, briefly. And as for these witnesses, we'll consider the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, obviously. And pease, you don't need to inform us; you need to inform Mr. Di Fazio or Mr. Wubben for that matter and then obviously we will have a revised witness scheduling.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And that's it for us. I want to wish you a happy holidays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm coming to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Just one housekeeping matter. We do have Prosecution's Exhibit 432 for everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I will be very brief because already we have had the indulgence and the very usual cooperation of all the staff here, so I will be very brief not to take your time. This is the last time we are meeting then before the recess. We will be reconvening on the 10th of January. This is going to be a recess during which some of us will be celebrating our festivities, some of us not. But in any case, it's a festive season for everyone and on behalf of Judge Brydensholt and on behalf of Judge Eser, on behalf also my staff I would like to wish you all the very best this festive season. May God bless you and we'll meet again on the 10th of January. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
